items.title: Helen Oakley Dance interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Diego, California, February 12, 1998
items.q: Rex, of course, who never really was able to show who he really was or how... But anyway that was great, great fun for a couple of years we made those small—

ctx.x: Exactly. The fact that Duke said it, that was enough you know. And so Irving Mills — I was brought into Mills’ office and that was the other half of my career, because as Stanley I think told you, Mills started these two record companies, Master Records was the top label, and Variety was the second. And I was the producer. I used to sit at this long table with about twenty accountants and people, and then they said to me, what have © Fillius Jazz Archive -8-

you to say? And I said, and so somebody said, “She did those Goodman things, and she did this and she did that you see. And so I said, “We ought to make the small band records.” And I knew Duke would agree you see, because Duke, amongst other things, he had a very good head for what could make a bit of money. Because he needed to. How was he going to keep going if he didn’t? And so of course that was a very good idea, because for two years, well it went on after I left them, we just made the small bands. You know…
